labels.caption: Sublet against the naive spend caps (policy seed 0): (a)~on weeks 301--316 (16 weeks), the median over the weeks of $r_0$ under each of the 13 lenders, and of the worst cases $W_0$ (over the five stress lenders) and $W_0^{+}$ (over these and the new ones), with bars from the min to the max over the weeks of $W_0$ and $W_0^{+}$; the grey line is the all-fallback cost; the latched and the slot-count cap $B(t)$ of critical-ratio renting are in (b)--(d) and the tables only. (b)~The run-time excess $\max_t \mathrm{ALG}(t)-C_{\mathrm{FB}}(t)-B(t)$ over $C_{\mathrm{FB}}(T)$ of every run of the confirmation weeks and of the sensitivity points, one column per policy under its marker, against Sublet's bound $C_{\mathrm{FB}}+B$ with $B$ Sublet's allowance, the same for every column whatever the cap's own limit $X$; shaded: above the bound; under each column the runs above it at some slot, out of the runs with a value; a run above the bound at some slot may end below it. For Sublet's runs read from the earlier studies the value is its envelope, an upper bound. 88 runs of a cap at $X=B(t)$ under one of the eleven lenders of $W_0^{+}$ or at $\rho=16$ end above the bound, having been above it at some slot; none of Sublet's 278 runs is above the bound, at the end or at some slot. (c), (d)~At the sensitivity points, Sublet and the caps at $X=B(t)$ (Critical-ratio renting, cap $B(t)$; Critical-ratio renting, latched cap $B(t)$; Critical-ratio renting, slot-count cap $B(t)$; and Greedy renting, cap $B(t)$): the median $r_0$ under the trace lender over weeks 301--304 and the median $W_0$ over weeks 301--302, each with its min--max. Every policy's values: Tables~\ref{tab:cap-runs}, \ref{tab:cap-margins}, \ref{tab:cap-binds}, \ref{tab:cap-modes}, \ref{tab:cap-mode-margins}, \ref{tab:cap-sens} and \ref{tab:cap-checks}; every run: cap\_runs.csv.
